function: Joint design of BS transmit beamformers and BDRIS reconfiguration matrix to maximize the minimum user rate (user fairness) with a learned policy (p. 1-3).
system: Multi-user downlink, BS ULA with Nt=50 antennas, fully connected beyond-diagonal reflecting RIS (BDRIS) with M=36 elements, near-field BS links, far-field BDRIS-user links, 2.4 GHz (p. 2, 4).
method: PPO actor-critic deep reinforcement learning, hidden layers of 128 and 64 neurons; reward is the minimum user rate; QR projection enforces the unitary BDRIS constraint (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulated LoS channels: near-field spherical-wave BS-user and BS-BDRIS (model of Bjornson and Sanguinetti), far-field BDRIS-user with path loss; no dataset or measurements (p. 2).
test_conditions: Same simulated setup for training and testing; users random in a 150 m x 150 m grid, 10 seeds; perfect/imperfect CSI; Nt and M varied (p. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: DDPG, SAC, RIS-ELAA DRL scheme of [16], ELAA-only DRL without RIS. Non-learned: ELAA with random transmit beamforming (p. 4).
metrics: Reward (minimum user rate), mean rate, outage probability from CDF of user rates, sum-rate, max-min rate, convergence episodes (p. 4-5).
complexity: Big-O order O((KNt+M^2)(n1+n2)+n1(n2+K)+M^3) from forward/backward passes plus QR; stated lower than the method of [8]; no runtime or FLOPs (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "The near field channel model is formulated in (1) shown at the bottom of the next page based on [11]"; custom LoS near-field and far-field models, no 3GPP TR 38.901, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "The impacts of the number of antennas Nt and the number of BDRIS elements M are also analyzed"; these are sweeps, network sizes depend on Nt and M (p. 4), and no test of one trained model on an unseen scenario is stated.
q3_support: p. 4: "is compared with Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG)" and SAC; p. 4: "an ELAA setup with random transmit beamforming vectors" as the non-learned baseline; compared on rates in Figs. 4, 5, 8.
q4_support: p. 4: "the total asymptotic complexity of the algorithm can be shown derived as" O(M^3 + (K Nt + M^2 + K) n1 + n1 n2 + (K Nt + M^2) n2).
q5_support: p. 4: "The experiment is repeated over 10 random seeds with hyperparameters in Table I"; own simulator, no code or data link or DOI, no public channel dataset.
notes: Area 3: the learned PPO policy outputs both the BS beamformers and the BDRIS matrix (p. 3). The Fig. 5 legend (p. 5) lists Proposed, ELAA only, RIS ELAA [16], Random, and Fig. 8 shows Proposed, RIS NF, NF Only, Random. The complexity of [8] is compared only analytically (p. 4).
